label: Mid Cycle / Valuation Compression
evidence: Reported fact: Q1 FY2026-27 real GDP growth was firm, indicating that the domestic cycle had not entered a broad contraction.
Reported fact: August CPI inflation moved close to the RBI's medium-term target area but food inflation remained higher than headline inflation.
Reported fact: the RBI held the repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance in August 2026, leaving the path of further easing data-dependent.
Market data: Nifty 50 and Nifty 500 price returns were negative over 1Y at the October 3, 2026 cutoff in the retained Yahoo-derived dataset.
Market data: sector leadership was narrow; pharma was resilient while IT and several domestic sectors showed weak trailing returns.
Our analysis: the combination of firm activity, uneven inflation and falling equity prices is more consistent with de-rating/earnings scrutiny than recession.
earnings: Data unavailable from reliable sources. Our analysis: verified aggregate forward earnings and revision breadth were not available; sector selection therefore emphasizes demand visibility, balance sheets and execution rather than unsupported consensus forecasts.
valuation: Data unavailable from reliable sources. Our analysis: no verified index forward P/E series is used. The regime label relies on observed price weakness alongside firm reported activity, not on an invented valuation multiple.
flows: Data unavailable from reliable sources. Our analysis: no cutoff-consistent FPI/DII flow series was verified, so flows are not used as a scoring input.
major_risks: Food or oil inflation delays easing and compresses consumer purchasing power.
Global risk-off conditions tighten financial conditions and pressure the rupee.
Public and private capex execution misses elevated expectations.
Earnings disappointments prolong de-rating in crowded quality and growth franchises.

positive: Domestic growth may prove more durable than weak trailing equity returns imply.
Selective margin recovery could emerge if input inflation moderates without demand damage.
negative: Markets may still be underpricing food/oil inflation persistence and the limits to rate cuts.
Without verified earnings revisions, apparent price correction may not equal valuation support.
